title.narrative: CoE Countering Economic Crime in Serbia

description.narrative:
Den föreslagna insatsen avser fortsättningen av det pågående programmet "Preventing Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in Serbia", som Sverige har stött sedan januari 2020. Programmet genomförs av Europarådet (CoE).
Det övergripande målet är att stärka huvudpelarna i AML/CFT-förebyggande och verkställighetsregimen i Serbien och uppdatera dess policy i linje med de nya europeiska och internationella standarderna, genom att fokusera på:
1. Förbättra mekanismer för att förebygga ML/FT som tillämpas av de serbiska myndigheterna, tillsynsorganen och den privata sektorn, i linje med identifierade risker och nya hot,
2. Förbättrad juridisk och operativ kapacitet för upptäckt, utredning och sanktionering av ML och TF och
3. System för återvinning och förvaltning av tillgångar optimerade för att säkerställa snabb identifiering och spårning av olagliga intäkter och effektivt bortskaffande av beslagtagna och konfiskerade tillgångar.

The contribution concerns the continuation of the ongoing program "Preventing Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in Serbia", which Sweden has supported since January 2020. The program is implemented by the CoE.
The overall objective is to strengthen the main pillars of AML/CFT prevention and enforcement regime in Serbia and update its policies in line with the new European and international standards, by focusing on:
1. Enhancing mechanisms for the prevention of ML/FT that are applied by the Serbian authorities, supervisory bodies and private sector, in line with identified risks and emerging threats,
2. Improved legal and operational capacities for detection, investigation and sanctioning of ML and TF and
3. Asset recovery and asset management systems optimized to ensure swift identification and tracing of illicit proceeds and effective disposal of seized and confiscated assets.

The overall objective of the intervention is to strengthen the main pillars of AML/CTF prevention and enforcement regime in Serbia and update its policies in line with the new European and international standards (revised recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force, 6th Anti-Money Laundering Directive and the new EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation). The overall objective is broken down into 3 outcomes, as follows:
Outcome 1: Enhanced mechanisms for prevention of economic crimes, including corruption and ML/TF, applied by the Serbian authorities and private sector, in line with identified risks and emerging threats;
Outcome 2: Improved legal and operational capacities for detection, investigation and sanctioning of corruption, money laundering and terrorism financing and
Outcome 3: Asset recovery and asset management systems optimized to ensure swift identification, tracing of illicit proceeds and effective confiscation and disposal of seized and confiscated assets.

The project "Countering Economic Crime in Serbia" has catalyzed a systemic shift across Serbia's Anti-Money Laundering/Counter-Terrorist Financing (AML/CFT) framework, from fragmented, compliancedriven practice toward coordinated, riskbased and datadriven implementation. Supervisory authorities, notably the Ministry of Domestic and Foreign Trade, Gaming Authority, Administration for the Prevention of Money Laundering (APML/FIU), National Bank of Serbia, and Ministry of Finance, transitioned from random, compliancedriven inspections to riskbased supervision grounded in quantified risk assessments. This enabled targeted, datadriven supervision in highrisk sectors, such as real estate, games of chance, and professional services. Law enforcement bodies, led by the Ministry of Interior (including the AntiCorruption Department and Service for Combatting Organized Crime) and prosecution, further strengthened the capacities to investigate and adjudicate corruption and financial crime through enhanced interagency cooperation, clearer financial forensics functions, improved plea bargain practice and more consistent sanctions. At the strategic level, the Government of Serbia, through the Coordination Body for AML/CFT and line ministries (notably the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Justice, and Ministry of Interior), demonstrated strengthened ownership and accountability through the adoption and implementation of a multisector, timebound Operational Plan for mitigating Money Laundering/Terrorist Financing/Proliferation Financing (ML/TF/PF) risks, embedding risk awareness into regular institutional planning.
Collectively, these sustained changes in supervision, investigation and policy coordination have fostered a proactive compliance culture aligned with European and international standards, culminating in Serbia's admission to the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) and a positive MONEYVAL Mutual Evaluation, which together confirm increased international trust in the resilience and credibility of Serbia's system for preventing and combating economic crime.
Key results achieved during the reporting period, both planned and unplanned, that have contributed to the overall progres towards agreed objectives are the following:
Policy and Institutional Framework
- Adoption of the Operational Plan for Mitigating Money Laundering/Terririst Financing/Proliferation Financing (ML/TF/PF) Risks (2025-2027), comprising 264 measures across supervisory authorities, law enforcement, prosecutorial services and private sector actors was a significant achievement during the reporting period. Together with the updated National Risk Assessment (NRA) and sectoral risk assessments completed earlier, it has morphed into the most comprehensive AML/CFT policy framework that Serbia has produced.
- National coordination mechanisms have been continuously strengthened, with broad involvement from ministries, supervisory authorities and judicial institutions. The MONEYVAL Mutual Evaluation Report (MER), adopted in December 2025, notes that Serbia has made significant progress in developing its anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CFT) systems, identifying positive developments in national risk assessment, international cooperation, financial sector supervision, and confiscation of criminal assets. It places Serbian AML/CFT system among the most effective among the rated countries.
- Regular awareness raising activities have reached over 300 private sector actors and approximately 140 representatives of the judiciary, prosecution and law enforcement, to ensure that NRA findings are translated into sector specific institutional measures.
Legislative Developments
Throughout the reporting period, several important legislative processes advanced:
- Amendments to the Law on Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing and the Law on Central Registry of Beneficial Owners were adopted in March 2025, further aligning Serbia's framework with FATF and EU requirements.
- A detailed assessment of Serbia's alignment with the EU Directive 2024/1640 was delivered, providing a comprehensive roadmap for future harmonization.
- A full review of the Law on Protection of Whistleblowers was done, generating over 70 recommendations aimed at improving legislative clarity, institutional mechanisms and protection in practice.
These developments demonstrate continued progress in aligning the legal framework with evolving international standards.
Capacity Building
Capacity building activities have been extensive, targeting several areas:
Supervisory capacity
- A new IT system for automated data collection and ML/TF risk analysis in the real estate sector was developed and put into operational use.
- Supervisory methodologies and tools have been substantially strengthened for real estate agencies, accounting companies, factoring companies, and games of chance organizers.
- Supervisors across these high risk sectors have completed specialized training, improving their ability to apply risk based offsite and onsite supervisory controls.
Private sector capacity
- More than 100 exchange offices were trained based on newly developed guidance for identification and reporting of suspicious transactions, including proliferation financing indicators.
Law enforcement and prosecution
- New Standard Operating Procedures for corruption investigations and financial enquiries were developed and tested through casebased exercises.
- A comprehensive analysis of plea bargaining in money laundering cases was finalized, including proposals for increased judicial oversight and safeguards.
- A needs assessment for financial forensic experts has been completed and capacity building efforts initiated accordingly.
Asset Recovery and Asset Management
The project has produced four technical papers that provide guidance on the management of complex seized assets, including crypto assets, high maintenance assets, volatile assets, and the interim use of seized vehicles. The implementation of these guidelines will help optimize operational practices and strengthen coordination among relevant authorities. They will also serve as a foundation for developing the necessary bylaws once the amendments to the Law on Seizure and Confiscation are completed.
These developments represent important progress in strengthening Serbia's asset management practices and reducing the risks associated with asset depreciation or mismanagement.
International Cooperation and Recognition
Serbia's admission to the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) in May 2025 marks a major step in the integration of its financial system into European payment structures, reflecting improved financial stability and application of AML/CFT measures.
The adoption of the positive MONEYVAL MER in December 2025 is expected to further reinforce this progress.
Unexpected positive results
- Higher than expected participation from both public and private sectors in policy and legislative consultations.
- Substantial ownership demonstrated by supervisory authorities and the Agency for Prevention of Corruption, which helped accelerate the uptake of guidance and tools.
- Broader public awareness of AML/CFT issues through outreach activities and media engagement.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
